title: Benchmarks and Leaderboards: Reading Public Numbers Critically
summary: Public benchmarks and arenas are how models get compared before you ever run them. This lesson explains what a benchmark score actually measures, why scores saturate and get contaminated, how arena ratings are computed from pairwise votes, and how to turn public numbers into a shortlist you then test yourself.
objectives: After this lesson you can describe a benchmark as task + metric + protocol and compute the error bar on a published score
Explain saturation and contamination, estimate how contamination inflates a score, and name the main detection methods
Fit a Bradley-Terry rating gap by hand from win counts and convert rating gaps into win probabilities
Read a leaderboard with confidence intervals, rank uncertainty and cost, instead of the rank alone
Decide which public results to trust for your own use case and design the private evaluation that settles the choice
prerequisites: Error bars and paired comparisons from [/learn/evaluation/comparing-systems](/learn/evaluation/comparing-systems), and LLM judges and their biases from [/learn/evaluation/llm-as-judge](/learn/evaluation/llm-as-judge). pass@k is introduced in [/learn/agents/traces-and-evaluation](/learn/agents/traces-and-evaluation).
